question: According to the 2011 census, what is the population density (per square km) of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**382.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the** 2011 census**, the population density of India is** 382 people per square kilometer. **
 
• Population density is calculated by** dividing the total population **of an area by its land area.
 
• India has a total land area of** 3.29 million square kilometers** and a population of **1.21 billion people,** making it the second-most populous country in the world after China.
 
• The high population density of India is a major challenge for the country as it puts pressure on** resources, infrastructure, and the environment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **15th Indian Census**, which took place in **2011, **was divided into **two phases:** **house listing and population enumeration.**
 
• The phase of house listing, which started on **1 April 2010,** involved gathering data on all structures. 
 
• In the first phase, data for the **National Population Register (NPR) **was also gathered.
 
• The Unique Identification Authority of India will use this data to issue a** 12-digit unique identification number** to every registered Indian resident.
 
• Between **February 9 and February 28, 2011**, the second population enumeration phase was carried out.
